note: Per-package LINE coverage floors, whole percent. CI fails if a package drops below its floor, or climbs more than `slack` points above it without recording the gain here. To move a floor: `npm run coverage:baseline`, or paste the block the failing CI run prints. Lowering one is allowed and deliberate — say why in the PR. NOTE: these floors are FORMATTER-SENSITIVE. Changing .oxfmtrc.json changes what counts as a line, so denominators move and percentages shift a point in either direction with no test change at all — the printWidth 120 pass moved four packages down one point and gave services/oauth two more lines. Regenerate the baseline in the same commit that changes formatting. See .github/scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs. | 2026-08-20: packages/outbound floor set to 53, the value CI measures, not the 56 measured locally. #239 recorded 56 from its worktree and main's CI reads 53 — a 3-line gap in one file (packages/outbound/src/index.ts, the SES relay), deterministic in BOTH environments across repeated runs, so it is an environment difference (CI's npm ci tree vs a dev checkout), not a regression: the only tests here are #233's two, unchanged. The floor takes the LOWER value on purpose — it still catches a real drop below 53, and it does not assert a number CI cannot reproduce. If the cause is ever found, raise it back. Slack widened 2→3 in the same commit for the same reason: with floor 53 a dev checkout reading 56 would otherwise fail as an 'unrecorded gain', so NEITHER value satisfied both environments at slack 2. Three points is the smallest window that lets one baseline be true in CI and in a working tree; narrow it again if the divergence is ever explained. | 2026-08-22: cli-go joins the ratchet. Go reports STATEMENTS, not lines, and go-coverage.mjs reports them in the `lines` slot — safe here because a ratchet compares a package against ITSELF over time, never against another package, and because the figure is the one `go tool cover -func` prints so a reader checking by hand sees the same number. `cli-go/main.go` is its own bucket at 0 because packageOf splits on two path segments and a 3-statement entrypoint has nowhere else to go (services/demo-keys and services/submit are already 0 for their own reasons).
